stories.headline: FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem: F1 drivers and staff won't be 'put at risk' over Middle East security situation
stories.summary: FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has defended the wait for clarity over how this year's Formula 1 season will end amid uncertainty over the Middle East security situation.
stories.body:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem defended the wait for clarity over how this year's Formula 1 season will end amid uncertainty over the Middle East security situation but told The Associated Press that drivers and team staff will not be put "at risk."

The F1 season is still scheduled to end with the Qatar Grand Prix on Nov. 29 and the season finale in Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6, but F1 has been examining potential alternative venues. A replacement finale at the Imola circuit in Italy is widely considered the likeliest option.

Ben Sulayem told the AP it remains "business as usual. We are not changing anything unless we have to," and he said he's in regular communication with F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali.

"Being from that part of the world, we can't jump the gun and just say, 'That's it, we are canceling' and then cancel," he added. "Are we going to allow our people, our staff, the drivers or the teams to go at risk? No, of course not. We will not. But we'll have also to listen to the governments and to the local promoter there."

F1 sets its own calendar and agreements with host venues, but as the governing body, the FIA must approve the schedule and any changes.

Iran has previously targeted Qatar and the UAE, which includes Abu Dhabi, as part of its response to U.S. airstrikes, and F1 called off the other two Middle East rounds earlier in the season -- in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

"And the wellbeing of my family being there and the UAE nationals and everyone that lives there comes as a priority," Ben Sulayem said.

He added that "for the time being, there is no emergency" in deciding a calendar for the 2027 season.

- Kimi Antonelli comes from 19th on the grid to win sensational home Italian Grand Prix

- Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix, first Italian to win in Monza since 1966 - as it happened

- Ferrari's Charles Leclerc reflects on battle with teammate Lewis Hamilton at Italian GP: 'We went too far'

If the season does finish in Imola, it will mean that Kimi Antonelli's quest to become F1's youngest champion could end with the party of a lifetime just down the road from his home city of Bologna.

When Antonelli raced there last year, he invited his family and his whole school class to see him at the track.

Antonelli, 20, moved 66 points clear in the title race with a statement victory at the Italian Grand Prix on Sunday, after an epic fight from the back of the grid.

stories.headline: Early bets for NFL Week 1: The plays we targeted once odds came out
stories.summary: What lines offered immediate value once odds came out? Here are four early bets to track.
stories.body:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is finally here, though odds for games have been out for some time.

The defending champion Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch to kick things off. We also get our first international game of the year, with this season's Super Bowl favorites, the Los Angeles Rams, facing off against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday in Melbourne, Australia.

Among the top games on Sunday's slate are the Buffalo Bills visiting the Houston Texans and the Minnesota Vikings hosting the Green Bay Packers. The Dallas Cowboys visit the New York Giants on "Sunday Night Football" to close out the day's action.

The Los Angeles Chargers are the biggest favorites of the week, laying 10 points against the Arizona Cardinals, and Sunday afternoon's Tampa Bay Buccaneers-Cincinnati Bengals matchup has the highest total of the week at 50.5.

Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on "Monday Night Football" (8:15 ET on ESPN/ABC) to close out the week.

Pamela Maldonado, Matt Bowen, Eric Moody and Joe Fortenbaugh looked at the early Week 1 odds and identified which ones are worth jumping on now before potential shifts later in the week.

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

Jacksonville Jaguars -7.5 vs. Cleveland Browns
Eric Moody: The Jaguars went 12-5 against the spread last season and covered 78% of their home games, while Cleveland was just 2-6 ATS on the road. Deshaun Watson is making his first regular-season start since 2024, and the Jaguars' defensive front should be able to pressure him and force the Browns to play from behind.

Last week: Steelers -4.5 vs. Browns (Steelers won, 23-9) -->

Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers UNDER 42.5 points

Joe Fortenbaugh: I know this might come as a surprise to many of you, but I'm not exactly bullish on the Tua Tagovailoa-led Falcons offense. The summer reports out of Atlanta were not favorable in terms of Tua's conditioning and willingness to throw the ball down the field. On the flip side, Pittsburgh might boast one of the most underrated defenses in the league, led by one of the most underrated coordinators in Patrick Graham. A 24-17 final would get us to the window.

New Orleans Saints +7 at Detroit Lions

Matt Bowen: I'll take the seven points with an ascending Saints team in Week 1. Quarterback Tyler Shough threw for 1,172 yards in his final four games as a rookie last season, and I really like his fit in Kellen Moore's offense. Shough is a rhythm thrower who can target the middle of the field versus the Lions' defensive scheme. The Saints can cover on the road.

Cardinals at Chargers UNDER 47.5

Pamela Maldonado: Arizona's offense might be better, but better doesn't mean high-scoring. Mike LaFleur has Jeremiyah Love as the centerpiece of a run-first approach designed to take pressure off an uninspiring quarterback room. The Chargers finished in the top 10 against the run last season and allowed the second-fewest red zone touchdowns, which could leave the Cardinals having trouble turning drives into seven points. Love gives Arizona explosiveness, but we're unlikely to see it against this defense.

stories.headline: Arsenal's Ezri Konsa 'loved' battle with England teammate Morgan Rogers in Chelsea clash
stories.summary: Ezri Konsa was delighted with his tackle on former teammate Morgan Rogers that brought a roar of approval from Arsenal fans during Sunday's 2-1 win over Chelsea.
stories.body:
Ezri Konsa was delighted with his tackle on former Aston Villa teammate Morgan Rogers that brought a roar of approval from Arsenal fans during Sunday's 2-1 win over Chelsea.

The champions were defending a one-goal lead late in the match when Rogers threatened to go clean through on goal until he was stopped in his tracks by a perfectly-timed challenge from Konsa on his home debut.

The Emirates Stadium crowd reacted with a cheer almost as loud the one that greeted the winning goal scored by Martin Odegaard early in the second half, as Mikel Arteta's side recovered from a goal down to maintain their perfect start to the season.

"I love duels," Konsa said. "As a defender, I think these are things you have to cherish.

"For me personally, I love a challenge. I love being in duels. I had a few today and I'm glad I came out on top.

"[Rogers] is a good friend of mine, but on the pitch, it's a different story. I saw the opportunity to go in and make the tackle and it came off."

Arsenal fell behind to a volley from Rogers after 77 seconds but hit back to level midway through the first half, Kai Havertz cutting in off the flank to beat Emiliano Martínez and score against his former team.

Chelsea's front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers were lively again but the visitors ultimately could not find their way past Konsa and co for a second time.

"I really enjoyed the occasion," the England defender said. "My first London derby and I thought the fans were fantastic, superb. They stayed behind us throughout the whole game; without them, these games are impossible.

"Conceding so early isn't great, and I know we take a lot of pride here in keeping clean sheets, but I thought the reaction was second to none, it was fantastic. It just goes to show the character and the mentality of this team."

Konsa, who made his debut in last week's 1-0 win away against his former side Villa, was in the side on Sunday in place of Cristhian Mosquera, who was injured, and long-term absentee William Saliba.

- Wayne Rooney: Arsenal defender Gabriel 'extremely lucky' to avoid red in Chelsea win

- Mikel Arteta: Arsenal can go to a 'higher level' than last season

"I felt right at home from day one," he said. "The boys have been top, the staff have been top. Like I said before in previous interviews, this style really suits me -- I love the boss' way of playing. The amount of quality that we have and the amount of quality I have around me makes things easier."

Arsenal are one of two teams in the league with perfect winning records after three matches. The Gunners are second on goal difference behind Manchester City.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Griezmann catapults Orlando into the playoff picture
stories.summary: With eight goal contributions in eight games since joining the Lions, Antoine Griezmann has turned around Orlando's season. That and more in ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While Nashville dropped points in a 0-0 draw against New York City on Friday, their biggest competitors for the Supporters' Shield slipped up, too. Both Vancouver and Miami failed to win, leaving Nashville with a 10-point lead atop the Shield race.

2. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 2

Despite taking an early lead, the Whitecaps quickly crumbled in a 3-1 home defeat against St. Louis. In what was, perhaps, their worst match of the season, Vancouver fell apart before halftime en route to losing to fellow contender out West for the second time in four games.

3. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 7

You couldn't have written a better script for St. Louis' Saturday night. Not only did new additions Rafael Navarro and Damion Downs make their debuts in the second half, but the visitors took the game to Vancouver and secured a 3-1 road victory. Doubt St. Louis' contender status at your own peril.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 3

Miami's Achilles heel is widely known: they're a team that gets easily scrambled in their own third. With two sloppy fouls conceding two penalties to Atlanta, Saturday's 2-2 draw with the Five Stripes was the latest example of Inter Miami's defensive play letting them down.

5. LAFC
Previous ranking: 5

Despite holding a one-goal lead heading into the intermission, LAFC's second-half concession saw them earn just a point on the road against Salt Lake. An unwillingness -- or inability -- to keep the ball late in games continues to bite for the Black & Gold.

6. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 6

After their scheduled meeting with D.C. United was postponed due to inclement weather, Cincinnati will have extra time to bed in their defensive reinforcements. That 4-0 loss to Nashville last time out still stings.

7. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 4

The good news? Chicago bagged four goals on Saturday, including one from Robert Lewandowski as he continues to find his place in the attack. The bad news? Chicago conceded four in a 4-4 draw with Toronto. It's safe to say Chicago are missing rising star Mbekezeli Mbokazi in the backline.

8. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 9

Up against a fearsome Nashville team, New York City manager Pascal Jansen opted for a fairly conservative approach on Friday. Ceding most of the ball, the Pigeons did well to keep Nashville scoreless, but they failed to create much danger themselves in a 0-0 home draw.

9. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Trailing by two goals at halftime, the Revs couldn't find a way to equalize against the Galaxy on their way to a 2-1 road defeat. While Carles Gil's penalty conversion got them on the board, questions remain about whether the options New England have placed around him will produce.

10. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

Despite having a man advantage for the final 20-plus minutes of the match, Houston had a hard time creating much of anything in their 0-0 road draw with Charlotte. While attacking questions remain for Ben Olsen's outfit, the Dynamo's string of shutdown defensive showings mark them as a team that must be taken seriously.

11. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

While Charlotte couldn't find a breakthrough during their 0-0 home draw with Houston, Allan Saint-Maximin looked like the best player on the field. Dean Smith's new left winger was at the center of nearly every threatening move and has the look of an MLS star.

12. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 12

Still winless in league play since May, RSL drew 2-2 with LAFC on Saturday. They created a slew of quality chances, but also proved too open in defensive transition as control and tactical balance still eludes them.

13. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 16

Antoine Griezmann continued his absolute tear with the lone goal in Orlando's 1-0 win over San Diego. Now with eight goal contributions in eight games since debuting for the Lions, Griezmann has quickly turned around Orlando's season: they're now above the playoff line in the East.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

If there's a debate about MLS's best striker, Petar Musa is doing his best to end it. The Croatia international managed two goals, including the game winner, and an assist in Dallas' 4-3 win over Kansas City. While the home side's focus lacked, Musa's certainly didn't.

15. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 15

Since league play resumed after the World Cup, the Union are yet to lose. Saturday's 2-0 victory over Montréal lengthened that streak of results to eight games, with six of them going down as wins. With yet another goal from Cavan Sullivan, Philadelphia are flying.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 15

Missing star midfielder Jeppe Tverskov due to a card suspension, San Diego's ball progression never turned into regular chances in a 1-0 road loss to Orlando. Without the Dane, the sophomore side simply can't carry the same threat going forward.

17. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 11

For a team that prides itself on effective defending, conceding three goals in the first half in a 5-4 loss to the Timbers was nowhere near good enough for Minnesota. Still, breakout striker Marcus Caldeira's brace could signal longer-term attacking improvement for a team fighting for a playoff spot.

18. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 20

The Galaxy marked Sergi Roberto's first MLS start with a 2-1 victory over New England. The former Barcelona man was a touch magnet in central midfield, helping his new team conduct play. If Roberto and Chucky Lozano, who notched an assist, maintain this form, the Galaxy won't be easily dismissed.

19. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 22

Josh Sargent appears to be finding his form in MLS. While the U.S. striker had a quiet start to life in Toronto, he notched a hat trick in a 4-4 draw with Chicago over the weekend. It was a top-tier showing from Sargent atop Robin Fraser's attacking structure that led to a point for the hosts.

20. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 19

Now below the playoff line out East following a 0-0 draw in Seattle, that Red Bull New York didn't do more in the summer transfer window is a major concern. Without any game-changing additions made to the squad before deadline day, it's difficult to see how Michael Bradley's team will rebound.

21. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 21

On Saturday, Sounders fans could breathe a collective sigh of relief upon seeing Cristian Roldan make his first start for the team since May. Still, the USMNT midfielder's return wasn't enough to see Seattle claim their first win in months. A 0-0 draw with the Red Bulls had to suffice.

22. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 23

With star striker Kevin Kelsy now off to Rangers in the Scottish Premiership, replacement Vincent Janssen didn't waste any time filling the Venezuelan's shoes. Janssen notched a hat trick in the Timbers' wild 5-4 home win over Minnesota.

23. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 18

It looked as if the Quakes' winless run, one that stretches all the way back to May, was going to come to an end on Saturday. That is, until Austin managed a 97th-minute equalizer and a victory turned into a 1-1 draw for San Jose. The Earthquakes are in a bad, bad place.

24. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 24

D.C.'s meeting with Cincinnati was postponed due to weather, leaving the club without a chance to break a five-game winless streak.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Thanks to an equalizer from Guilherme Biro deep in second-half stoppage time, Austin secured a 1-1 draw against San Jose. The result marked four straight games without a loss in league play for the Texas capital club.

26. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 27

It didn't take Santi Rodriguez long to open his account in Columbus. The former New York City star bagged the opening goal for the Crew in a 3-0 victory over Colorado. With a remade attack, could this team make a late push for a spot in the postseason?

27. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 26

After trading Navarro to St. Louis and adding new pieces to the attack just before deadline day, the Rapids were nowhere near full strength in a 3-0 loss to the Crew. Colorado will have to wait for their new pieces to arrive and integrate to reach their full potential.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

At last, there are signs of life in Atlanta. During their 2-2 draw with Miami, new striker Breel Embolo made his debut and scored a late equalizer from the spot. Elsewhere, young defensive midfielder Mauricio Amaro made his first MLS appearance and looked extremely comfortable amid his new surroundings.

29. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 29

Back to the bottom of the East after falling 2-0 in Philadelphia, it's difficult to see Montréal climbing the standings anytime soon. Even with Alexis Sánchez in the lineup, this team is still light on talent.

30. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 30

Although they managed one of their best attacking outings of the year, spurred on by new winger André Luiz's first start, Kansas City couldn't hold on for a point in Dallas. They fell 4-3 thanks to a late penalty by Musa.

stories.headline: NBA offseason recap, early 2026-27 season previews by team
stories.summary: We're looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the regular season by rolling out one team profile each weekday through Sept. 18.
stories.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Central Division

Milwaukee Bucks: Sept. 7
Key additions: Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, Caris LeVert

Key retentions: Gary Trent Jr.

Key subtractions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis

After 13 seasons, the Giannis era ended in Milwaukee with a mega trade to the Heat -- and the 2026-27 season will mark a major shift for the rebuilding franchise.

The Bucks hired coach Taylor Jenkins to establish a culture. They added four new players from Miami, including former All-Star and Wisconsin native Tyler Herro, and selected Brayden Burries with the No. 10 pick in June.

The Bucks will enter the season with an ill-fitting mix of players and low expectations, but they have the luxury to see what sticks long term. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Bucks offseason recap/season preview

Chicago Bulls: Sept. 8

Cleveland Cavaliers: Sept. 9

Indiana Pacers: Sept. 10

Detroit Pistons: Sept. 11

Southeast Division

Miami Heat: Aug. 31
Key additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Nick Richards

Key retentions: Andrew Wiggins, Simone Fontecchio

Key subtractions: Tyler Herro, Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis

Heat president Pat Riley landed the superstar he'd been searching for since LeBron James left Miami in 2016. Antetokounmpo is in the fold, and Miami is ready to contend for another title with the two-time MVP. Antetokounmpo is just as motivated to win his second title and remind everyone that he can be the best player in the league.

In the trade, the Heat gave up key players such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez and did not bring back Powell in free agency. They landed Thompson to a two-year, $13 million deal after the four-time champion sharpshooter worked out a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. Miami also added Portis and Hardaway, but the team is still looking to bolster the roster around Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Heat offseason recap/season preview

Washington Wizards: Sept. 1
Key additions: AJ Dybantsa, Khris Middleton, Deandre Ayton, Tre Mann

Key subtractions: Cam Whitmore, D'Angelo Russell, Jaden Hardy

Key retentions: Trae Young

The Wizards got their jump on this pivotal offseason by acquiring Trae Young and Anthony Davis last season in trades.

Those were their two big moves and then came the big prize for losing 65 games last season - winning the lottery and drafting AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick.

Ready to start winning games this season after losing 60 or more games in each of the past three years, Washington gave Young a four-year, $212 million contract. The Wizards added veterans like Khris Middleton and Deandre Ayton to bolster the depth behind their young core featuring the likes of Dybantsa, Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George, Tre Johnson and Will Riley. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Wizards offseason recap/season preview

Charlotte Hornets: Sept. 2
Key additions: F Naz Reid, G Grayson Allen, G Dennis Schroder, F Royce O'Neale, F Dorian Finney-Smith

Key retentions: G Coby White

Key subtractions: G LaMelo Ball, F Miles Bridges, G Josh Green, G Tre Mann

After enjoying their best season in a decade, the Hornets sharply changed course with the surprising decision to trade Ball, their franchise guard, to the Timberwolves.

Given that Ball was a borderline All-Star on a max contract, Charlotte opted for a "Moneyball" approach in hopes of avoiding the perpetual mediocrity that tripped up Trae Young's Atlanta Hawks in the recent past.

With Ball and starting forward Miles Bridges moved in separate deals aimed at collecting future draft assets and improving its cap flexibility, Charlotte is now the only team that doesn't have a single player on the books for at least $25 million next season. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Hornets offseason recap/season preview

Atlanta Hawks: Sept. 3
Key additions: Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Kingston Flemings, Devin Carter, Ryan Nembhard, Zuby Ejiofor, Henri Veesaar

Key retentions: CJ McCollum, Jock Landale

Key subtractions: Zaccharie Risacher, Jonathan Kuminga, Gabe Vincent, Keaton Wallace

Atlanta continued to move forward from the Trae Young trade last season by being opportunistic this offseason.

The Hawks acquired Dort and Wiggins in separate trades from the Oklahoma City Thunder to add more help around emerging star Jalen Johnson. The Hawks also kept McCollum on a one-year, $21 million deal and drafted Flemings eighth overall.

Atlanta is loaded with young wings looking to take a step forward under Quin Snyder like Nickeil Alexander-Walker did last season in winning Most Improved Player. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Hawks offseason recap/season preview

Orlando Magic: Sept. 4
Key additions: C Nikola Vucevic, G Izaiyah Nelson

Key subtractions: F Moritz Wagner, G Jett Howard

Key retentions: F Jonathan Isaac, G Jevon Carter

The Magic's biggest move this offseason was hiring Sean Sweeney to replace Jamahl Mosley.

Orlando also brought Nikola Vucevic back on a one-year, $3.9 million deal since trading him in 2021 and will use his ability to score and shoot to space the floor for Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane.

The Magic blew a 3-1 lead over top-seeded Detroit in the first round of the playoffs after Wagner went down due to injury and were in desperate need of someone who can get easier baskets and make outside shots. Vucevic should help. Moe Wagner departed for Brooklyn via free agency, separating Franz from his brother for the first time in his pro career. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Magic offseason recap/season preview

Pacific Division

Los Angeles Lakers: Aug. 24
Key additions: C Walker Kessler, F Sandro Mamukelashvili, G Quentin Grimes, G Collin Sexton, F Kevon Looney, F Matisse Thybulle, G Cameron Carr

Key retentions: G Austin Reaves

Key subtractions: F LeBron James, C Deandre Ayton, G Marcus Smart, F Rui Hachimura, G Luke Kennard, C Jaxson Hayes

James informed the Lakers he would not be returning for next season on June 30. Two days later, the team transformed the roster, with Doncic squarely as the focal point.

The biggest addition -- literally and figuratively -- is 7-foot-2 center Kessler, acquired in a sign-and-trade deal with the Utah Jazz. L.A. sent two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and pick swaps in 2028 and 2030, not to mention a four-year, $130 million contract, to acquire him.

Mamukelashvili, Grimes, Sexton, Looney and Thybulle also signed with the Lakers, and free agent Ziaire Williams and first-round pick Carr bolster the team's young prospect pool of Adou Thiero, Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

The most important move, though, came when Reaves, coming off a career season in which he averaged 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game, signed a four-year, $180 million extension.

When the dust settled, it was a dramatic roster overhaul in what could prove to be one of the most consequential summers in franchise history, with the team also being sold for the second time in 14 months, this time to venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger, who bought the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Lakers offseason recap/season preview

LA Clippers: Aug. 25
Key additions: Rui Hachimura, Keaton Wagler, Brandon Ingram (TBD), Gradey Dick (TBD)

Key retentions: Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal

Key subtractions: Kawhi Leonard (TBD), Nicolas Batum, Bogdan Bogdanovic, John Collins

What started as a reconfiguration at the trade deadline -- acquiring Darius Garland from Cleveland for James Harden and Bennedict Mathurin from Indiana for Ivica Zubac -- turned into a complete overhaul this summer after the Clippers let Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum and John Collins walk.

Their biggest move, however, was trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft picks, but that deal is in limbo pending the investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the team relating to Leonard's Aspiration endorsement deal.

In the meantime, LA added Illinois guard Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the draft and signed Hachimura away from the crosstown Lakers with a two-year, $28 million deal. And in a surprise move, Bradley Beal -- after declining his $5.6 million contract option for next season in June to test free agency -- ended up re-signing on a two-year, $13.2 million deal in mid-August to stay with the Clippers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Clippers offseason recap/season preview

Golden State Warriors: Aug. 26
Key additions: Yaxel Lendeborg, Brandon Williams, Georges Niang

Key subtractions: Quinten Post, Pat Spencer

Key retentions: Draymond Green, Al Horford, Kristaps Porzingis, Gary Payton II, De'Anthony Melton

The Warriors opted for flexibility and stability over a larger shake-up around Curry. Their much-publicized recruitment of James never gained much traction.

They brought back their veteran frontcourt trio (Green, Horford, Porzingis), but kept them all on short-term maneuverable contracts. They opted for the fit of Melton over a pursuit of scoring guard Anfernee Simons. Their big addition is Lendeborg, the 23-year-old rookie wing who they will rely upon to be a high-minute, high-impact rotation player immediately.

In the bigger picture, they protected their draft pick cupboard and lined up their books to have an ocean of cap space as they peer a bit deeper into the future while their core ages. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Warriors offseason recap/season preview

Phoenix Suns: Aug. 27
Key additions: F Miles Bridges, F Koa Peat, G Luke Kennard

Key subtractions: G Grayson Allen, F Royce O'Neale

Key retentions: F Dillon Brooks, G Collin Gillespie, C Mark Williams, G Jordan Goodwin

Phoenix followed up its surprising season with a series of moves to mostly keep its team intact, with some adjustments around the margins.

The Suns re-signed Gillespie (four years, $48 million), Williams (three years, $38 million), Goodwin (three years, $19 million) and Brooks (three years, $73 million) to new deals and made a major splash by trading Allen and O'Neale to the Charlotte Hornets for Bridges. And despite not having a pick until No. 47 in the second round of the 2026 draft, Phoenix was able to acquire Arizona player Peat -- who averaged 14.1 points on 52.8% shooting as a freshman for the Wildcats and was key to their Final Four run. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Suns offseason recap/season preview

Sacramento Kings: Aug. 28
Key additions: G Darius Acuff Jr., F Alex Karaban, G Emanuel Sharp

Key subtractions: G DeMar DeRozan, G Russell Westbrook

Key retentions: F Precious Achiuwa

Perry, currently in the organization's power seat, is continuing a steady transition toward the younger core he has drafted. Arkansas guard and No. 7 pick Acuff is the spotlight name on a roster populated with six players in their first two NBA seasons.

But they still have notable high-minute holdovers from the past regime, including Murray, Malik Monk, LaVine and Sabonis. Of those four, Murray appears the most locked-in as a stable member of the team's long-term vision. Perry explored trades for Monk, LaVine and Sabonis over the past year, but didn't value the proposed returns, and the three are expected to open the season in Sacramento. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Kings offseason recap/season preview

Northwest Division

Portland Trail Blazers: Aug. 17
Key additions: G Ja Morant, F Jeremy Sochan

Key retentions: C Robert Williams III

Key subtractions: F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, G Matisse Thybulle

Although the Blazers were the only team that sat out June's draft by not making a pick, they will add two high-profile guards to a rotation that otherwise looks very similar to last season. Minnesota also re-signed wing Clark and guard Hyland and acquired the 6-foot-6 Evans out of Duke with the No. 33 pick in the draft.

They sent Isaiah Joe to Detroit and traded Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort to Atlanta in separate moves, eroding their depth.

General manager Sam Presti made clear in an interview with The Oklahoman that the impression he's been given from ownership is "the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be re-allocated to future teams."

But retaining the 23-year-old would have been expensive -- via either a sky-high luxury tax bill or a salary-slashing move to get off an important veteran and generate more breathing room for a new deal.

Memphis is in a full-blown youth movement, as 21-year-old forward GG Jackson is now the longest-tenured player on the roster. stories.headline: Sky owner calls Kanter Freedom's free speech lawsuit 'meritless'
stories.summary: Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter called a lawsuit filed by Enes Kanter Freedom "meritless and frivolous."
stories.body:
Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter called a lawsuit filed by Enes Kanter Freedom "meritless and frivolous" Friday afternoon.

Kanter Freedom alleged that his First Amendment rights were violated when he was removed from a Sky home game Aug. 23 and then banned from attending Sky games at the arena. The former NBA player was removed from the building after getting in a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter against the Indiana Fever. He was sitting courtside in a black T-shirt that read: "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

Kanter Freedom put up his arms and began to walk toward the court from his baseline seat as he and Cloud exchanged words. He stepped past media camera operators to approach the floor; security stopped him and subsequently ejected him. Alter had previously explained that Kanter Freedom made himself "the potential to be a threat" by stepping toward the court and players.

A 15-page complaint was filed Thursday in the Northern District of Illinois Eastern Division and listed the defendants as the Sky, the city of Chicago, and Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, which owns and operates Wintrust Arena.

"This lawsuit is meritless and frivolous," Alter said in a statement Friday. "Freedom's claim that he was removed from Wintrust Arena due to his speech is false. As his own complaint acknowledges, he wore the shirt in question for multiple hours without any contact with security. Security removed Freedom only after he violated fan code of conduct by rising from his seat, gesturing at a player, and stepping toward the court.

"Freedom was removed for his conduct, not his speech. We look forward to the truth prevailing in court."

Kanter Freedom has inserted himself in the political realm in recent years and has been vocal in the national debate sparked by Fever guard Sophie Cunningham's comments regarding transgender athletes. He and former NBA player Royce White recently declared themselves women and eligible to play in the WNBA. They are not eligible to play in the league, multiple sources told ESPN.

On social media, Kanter Freedom posted that he was "peacefully exercising" his First Amendment rights.

"My T-shirt did what the whole WNBA apparently couldn't: define a woman," Kanter Freedom wrote. "No threats. No violence. Just biology. And somehow, that required a security escort.

"You don't have to agree with my speech but you don't get to silence me for it. I will not be intimidated. I will not be silenced. I will continue to stand for women and defend free speech."

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey forward tiers: Who to draft and when to take them
stories.summary: Use these forward tiers to help you plan out your fantasy hockey draft strategy.
stories.body:
Picture the boarding line at the airport.

They call Group 1, and here's the thing about Group 1, it does not matter one bit where in that group you're standing. First person or last, you're strolling on with your bag and your pick of the overhead bin. Everyone in the group is, functionally, the same.

Then they call Group 2 ... still totally fine, still getting your bag up top. Group 3, you're eyeing the bins nervously, but at least you're all in the same boat. Er, plane.

By the time they're calling Group 6, you're handing your carry-on to the gate agent and hoping to see it in the next time zone -- but so is everyone else in your group.

That drop, from group to group, real and steep, with near-total equality inside each group? That's a tier list. That's the whole idea. And that's how you should draft.

Here's why it saves you at a draft. Say you've got your eye on one guy, and the two picks ahead of you snap him and the player right next to him up. On a flat ranking, you panic. Scramble down to whatever's left with the clock screaming at you. But if you already knew those two were sitting in the same boarding group as three other players you rated just as highly? You don't flinch. You wave the next one aboard and you've lost nothing.

That's the magic -- you stop making 150 individual decisions and start making a handful of "anyone in this group is fine" ones. It's the same reason you don't need to stampede toward the jetway when your group is called. Everyone in it lands in the same place.

The fantasy forward groups below are mine. My projections, my drop-offs, my problem when I'm wrong. They aren't the official in-game ranks you'll see inside the ESPN Fantasy Hockey.

These come from my own projections: a base of each player's three-year average, a sprinkle of how comparable players the same age have fared across the past 15 seasons, and a dash of manual adjustment for the spots where my gut overrules the math. The projected ESPN standard points sit right next to each name below, so you can see exactly where I've got everyone slotted.

Note: Points based on the ESPN standard scoring system.

stories.headline: A bit 'unfair': Sharks players unhappy over finals call
stories.summary: Cronulla firebrand Addin Fonua-Blake says it's unfair that Saturday night's home final cannot be played at Shark Park, despite Peter V'landys' insistence the decision has the support of a lot of the club's fans.
stories.body:
Cronulla firebrand Addin Fonua-Blake says it's unfair that Saturday night's home final cannot be played at Shark Park, despite Peter V'landys' insistence the decision has the support of a lot of the club's fans.

The Sharks received a massive personnel boost on Monday, with Braydon Trindall training and Fonua-Blake revealing he expected the star five-eighth to play.

But Cronulla players were also left to admit their disappointment at not being allowed to face North Queensland at Shark Park, with the game instead set for Allianz Stadium.

The NRL's decision comes after years of debate around finals venues, with Shark Park the most scrutinised given its currently-reduced capacity of 13,500 amid an ongoing leagues' club reconstruction.

Cronulla bosses had been hopeful the fact the club were playing the Cowboys would allow the game to be played at a suburban ground, given the likelihood of fewer away fans.

But that hope was officially snuffed on Sunday, raising questions over whether Shark Park would ever host a finals match again.

"It's not ideal," Fonua-Blake said.

"You work so hard during the year to get a home semi and for it to be taken away, it's unfair.

"It's the incentive for finishing higher on the ladder, and to not get it, it's a bit unfair."

The NSW State of Origin prop said his concern was driven by the fact most clubs could play at their home stadium.

"To play in front of your home crowd, it feels like you have a 14th player on the field sometimes," he said.

"It's a bit unfair, but what can you do? The call has been made above our heads.

"We've just got to cop it and get ready to go out and put in a good performance this weekend."

The NRL changed its rules at the end of last season to give it the ultimate say on where finals would be played.

But Australian Rugby League Commission chairman V'landys insisted on Monday that the door was not forever shut on all suburban grounds hosting finals in the future.

"We're going to look at every game on its merits," said V'landys, who is also currently acting as NRL executive chairman.

"We still want to try to keep the suburban grounds as much as possible.

"But when their capacity and their facilities aren't there at the standard you want, you've got to shift them.

"Unfortunately, at the moment, Shark Park, I don't think anyone can argue, isn't that facility where you're giving the fan the ultimate experience."

When asked how Cronulla took the news, V'landys said it had been made with the club's fans in mind.

"A lot of Sharks fans wanted to go to Allianz, believe it or not," he said.

"And we wanted to accommodate them. Plus, we wanted to accommodate a lot more fans.

"Why would you have a billion-dollar venue sitting there doing nothing? Why not give fans the ultimate comfort and the ultimate experience?"

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc Italian GP duel 'not good for the team,' says Ferrari boss
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has been warned that his in-fighting with Charles Leclerc at Ferrari "is not good for the team."
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has been warned that his in-fighting with Charles Leclerc at Ferrari "is not good for the team."

Hamilton and Leclerc clashed at the opening corner of Sunday's Italian Grand Prix, with the former accusing his teammate of pushing him off the track.

The first-lap incident at Ferrari's home event escaped any punishment from the stewards.

But Hamilton said that the Ferrari fans "should not be worried about me" following Leclerc's claim that both drivers were at fault for the flashpoint which cost Hamilton six positions.

"There was no 'we' in it," said Hamilton as he laid the blame at Leclerc's door. "I don't race dirty, I've always raced clean and fairly and always left space."

The 41-year-old also called for a "written rules of engagement."

Hamilton's former rival, the 2016 world champion Nico Rosberg, although conceding that the British driver was "aggressive," felt that the clash was "100% Charles' fault."

Leclerc crashed out on the next lap while Hamilton finished only sixth to leave his hopes of catching Kimi Antonelli and claiming a record eighth world championship all but over.

And after overseeing a torrid result for Ferrari, team principal Fred Vasseur said: "We will have time to discuss it [with the drivers]. But the outcome of Turn 1-2 is not good for the team."

Hamilton is now 76 points adrift of Antonelli -- the equivalent of more than three wins -- with just 10 scheduled rounds remaining.

But Vasseur also defended his decision not to hand Hamilton priority over Leclerc in the fight for the title.

- Kimi Antonelli comes from 19th on the grid to win sensational home Italian Grand Prix

- Spanish Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Madrid, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Ferrari's Charles Leclerc reflects on battle with teammate Lewis Hamilton at Italian GP: 'We went too far'

Hamilton held a 28-point lead over Leclerc in the standings prior to Monza, and is 36 clear of the Monégasque heading into this weekend's inaugural round in Madrid.

In the aftermath of Sunday's race, Hamilton said it is now "far too late" for Ferrari to throw their weight behind him.

But Vasseur continued: "A good comparison that I made was that last year [Oscar] Piastri was leading the championship at this stage of the season and if McLaren put everything on Piastri [instead of teammate Lando Norris], Max Verstappen would have been champion.

"At one stage you have to take a decision, but it was too early to take a decision before Monza. Every single team principal in the world would love to let them race. To freeze positions is not an easy call. Now I will have time to discuss it with the drivers."

stories.body:
AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is the No. 1 option to replace Enzo Fernández in Chelsea's midfield, while USMNT and AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is attracting interest from clubs in Saudi Arabia. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are at the front of the queue to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, TEAMtalk reports. The Blues see the 23-year-old as their No. 1 option to replace Enzo Fernández in midfield -- having started this season with a pair of full backs in midfield -- and are set to explore whether a move for him can be secured in January. Bournemouth could be open to an offer due to Scott's contractual situation, as he will enter the final year of his deal next summer after previously turning down an extension at the Vitality Stadium.

- AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is attracting interest from clubs in Saudi Arabia, Football Insider reports. The Saudi Pro League is keeping close tabs on the situation of the 25-year-old USMNT international, who could part ways with the Ligue 1 club in a matter of days after being left out of the team's UEFA Conference League squad. Les Monegasques have been keen to offload Balogun due to their financial situation and remain intent on moving him on after his €40 million switch to Everton broke down on deadline day.

- Liverpool, Arsenal, and Manchester City are monitoring the situation of AS Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, according to TEAMtalk. The three clubs are reportedly among several that sent scouts to watch the 22-year-old in Friday's 2-1 Ligue 1 victory over Paris Saint-Germain. A race is now developing for Camara's signature after his €55 million move to Chelsea broke down on deadline day, and it looks as though the Blues could face strong competition if they make a fresh approach for him in January.

- Real Madrid striker Endrick is on the radar of AC Milan, according to Calciomercato. The Rossoneri made an attempt to sign the 20-year-old on loan in the summer transfer window, with plans now being drawn up to make a new offer in January that will include an option to become permanent. Endrick is yet to feature for Los Blancos this season after a loan spell at Lyon last season where he scored five goals and provided seven assists in 16 league games.

- Former Chelsea forward Hakim Ziyech has agreed terms with Botafogo, according to UOL. The 33-year-old free agent is reported to have agreed a two-year deal with the club, and an announcement is expected this week once he signs officially. Ziyech was released by Wydad Casablanca on Sunday and was keen to move quickly to secure a switch to the Brasileirao.

stories.headline: Champions League Power Rankings before MD1: Who's No. 1?
stories.summary: It's time for the UEFA Champions League! Before each matchday, our panel of experts and voters will rank the top 10 teams in the field to give you a sense of the contenders and pretenders. Where does your club rank?
stories.body:
The UEFA Champions League is back for another season and, fresh off the Aug. 27 draw, we have storylines and drama galore across the 36-team league phase.

A few big clubs -- including Liverpool and Real Madrid -- received gentle draws when it came to top-tier opponents from Pot 1, while the likes of Barcelona, Manchester United and Aston Villa might cringe at their fixture lists given a slew of difficult opponents. New Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has not one, but two reunions with clubs he has managed in the past, as his side must face Inter Milan and AS Roma between now and the end of January.

Every team will have one thing in common: the desire to finish in the top 24 and safely pass through to the knockout stages, where anything can happen.

In a new feature recurring at the start of every game week, ESPN will rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who our experts think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings before Matchday 1.

But first, some brief methodology
As we have done with other competitions, we're asking 19 of our reporters around the world to assess the UEFA Champions League from a contenders vs. pretenders perspective. Our panel were asked to assess the 36-team field in the league phase from No. 1 (meaning the trophy is theirs) to No. 10 (the cool outsider's pick for a tournament shock), with their ballots compiled into the collective top-10 ranking below.

We will ask our reporters to vote before each matchday to get an updated sense of their confidence about those clubs expecting to win it all in Madrid on June 5.

UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 1

1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN

Home opponents: Barcelona, AS Roma, Galatasaray, Slovan Bratislava

Away opponents: Man City, Aston Villa, Villarreal, Como

MD1: vs. Slovan Bratislava, Wednesday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

The back-to-back defending champs were as unanimous as it gets in our inaugural vote, picking up nine of 19 first-place votes -- only Arsenal, with five, came remotely close -- and were never ranked below fourth across our panel of experts. That's the definition of "team to beat" -- and having a gentle Ligue 1 campaign should mean they are able to pour their whole selves into trying to be the first team since Real Madrid (2016-18) to win three straight European titles.

The summer transfer window didn't quite go according to plan -- top target Yan Diomande chose Real Madrid, and Bradley Barcola was moved on to Liverpool -- but PSG did add quality depth in Ferran Torres (from Barcelona) and Lucas Digne (from Aston Villa) as well as young talent (Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche) that should excel in this format. Oh, and don't forget that manager Luis Enrique still has two of the world's best -- Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and reigning Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé -- who are keen to continue their all-world form.

While MD1 should yield a routine win, PSG are coming off a home defeat to Monaco this past weekend, and a pair of tougher tests await in MD2 (Man City away) and MD3 (Barcelona at home) that should give us a deeper sense of how well-equipped they are to defend their crown.

2. ARSENAL

Home opponents: Real Madrid, Borussia Dortmund, Lille, Sabah FK

Away opponents: Bayern Munich, Real Betis, Napoli, Slavia Prague

MD1: at Napoli, Wednesday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

Is this the Gunners' year? Our voters certainly consider Mikel Arteta & Co. as their consensus No. 2 -- though they did pick up five first-place votes -- and it makes sense considering that they clinched the Premier League title last year for the first time in over 20 years, and spent the summer trying to beef up an already formidable squad.

Though some quality depth in Gabriel Martinelli (to Al Hilal), Gabriel Jesus (to Barcelona) and Leandro Trossard (to Besiktas) has moved out this offseason, the additions of defender Ezri Konsa (from Aston Villa), midfielder Bruno Guimarães (from Newcastle United) and winger Christos Tzolis (from Club Brugge) offer proven quality and the kind of "win-now" experience that Arteta has been coveting. After all, this is their time, so why not make the most of it?

A tricky schedule has curtailed some enthusiasm among our voters -- Arsenal face arguably the toughest teams from the top pot as well as the best of Germany, Italy and France further down the ladder -- as their Premier League campaign will be extremely unforgiving, but the Gunners' defense and set-piece prowess should go a long way in Europe.

3. BAYERN MUNICH

Home opponents: Arsenal, Real Betis, Bodo/Glimt, Slavia Prague

Away opponents: Atlético Madrid, Man United, Lille, Viking FK

MD1: vs. Bodo/Glimt, Thursday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

Like PSG, the Bavarians are expected to be a dominant force in Europe thanks to the relative ease of their domestic campaign, and it's easy to see why. Led by future Ballon d'Or winner Michael Olise -- ESPN's Bill Connelly is calling it for 2027! -- an array of attacking talent and a gentle schedule of league-phase opponents, Vincent Kompany & Co. have their destiny in their own hands.

With Olise at the No. 10 behind striker Harry Kane (64 goals last season) and winger Luis Díaz (26 goals/19 assists, all comps in 2025-26), the path is there for a first European title since 2019-20. Don't read too much into their first scoreless Bundesliga game in over 18 months as they drew 0-0 with Schalke; if anything, that'll make them come out stronger this week when they begin their European odyssey.

4. BARCELONA

Home opponents: Man City, Aston Villa, Feyenoord, Como

Away opponents: PSG, Sporting CP, Galatasaray, Sabah FK

MD1: vs. Feyenoord, Wednesday, 12:45 p.m. ET / 5:45 p.m. BST

The last of our true Tier 1 -- teams our voters scored in the top four far above the field -- is Barcelona, and it's easy to see why. Hansi Flick's side romped to a LaLiga title last season thanks to a high-octane attack led by Lamine Yamal, but several of his co-conspirators (Torres, Robert Lewandowski, on-loan Marcus Rashford) have since departed as Flick attempts to revamp and evolve in real time.

Making things easier is the summer arrival of Rodri, a Ballon d'Or winner who is simply peerless in that deeper No. 6 midfield role responsible for knitting defense with attack. His presence isn't entirely without risk -- can the 30-year-old's fitness hold up in a high-octane pressing system like Flick's? -- but it does go a long way to freeing up Yamal & Co. to dominate further up field. The early season returns have been promising -- four straight wins to open the season, scoring five goals in three of those victories and outscoring opponents 17-2 -- as Raphinha (six goals in 2026-27) and new arrival Anthony Gordon (four assists in 244 minutes) create reliable chaos around goal.

The biggest question with Barça is always about their defense, which has been too naive to help them win in Europe. Young center back Pau Cubarsí is coming off a transcendent World Cup, but only full back João Cancelo came in this summer to bolster things at the back. Will it be enough?

5. REAL MADRID

Home opponents: Inter Milan, PSV Eindhoven, RB Leipzig, LASK

Away opponents: Arsenal, AS Roma, Shakhtar Donetsk, AEK Athens

MD1: vs. Inter Milan, Tuesday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

Mourinho is back at Real Madrid to restore stability and luster to a proud, demanding club, having won the UEFA Champions League twice before -- with FC Porto in 2003-04, a win that put him on the map, and Inter Milan in 2009-10. Our voters have Inter as the clear leader in our second tier of contenders, with only one first-place vote and one other ballot placing them higher than fourth.

A wobbly start to the season might be partially to blame for this perceived slight in the standings -- after a 90th-minute winner to beat Espanyol in their season opener, Madrid thumped Real Sociedad and Malaga before losing at Real Betis -- but also, voters aren't confident Mourinho has the required maturity and temperament to keep his superstars motivated if results aren't going their way. This team will go as far as Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham can take them.

A decisive performance -- and win -- over Inter would go a long way to putting Madrid's critics in their place.

6. MANCHESTER CITY

Home opponents: PSG, Sporting CP, Napoli, AEK Athens

Away opponents: Barcelona, FC Porto, RB Leipzig, Lens

MD1: at FC Porto, Tuesday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

Our voters put City firmly in the middle of our contenders for the title given the scope and scale of turnover at the Etihad this summer, and it remains to be seen whether the replacements can live up to their predecessors up and down the squad. Can Enzo Maresca coach this crew to the level Pep Guardiola did for nearly a decade? Can Elliot Anderson (from Nottingham Forest), young Ayyoub Bouaddi (from Lille), and deadline day arrival Enzo Fernández (from Chelsea) fill the Rodri-shaped hole in midfield following the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner's sudden move to Barcelona?

Our voters aren't sure, and a schedule filled with threats at every turn -- Napoli and RB Leipzig might be the toughest draw from Pot 3 -- has also added some skepticism to their chances, but as long as Erling Haaland (41 goals, 10 assists last season in all competitions) and Rayan Cherki (17 assists last term) continue to make merry in the attacking third, they should be a tough opponent.

7. INTER MILAN

Home opponents: Liverpool, Club Brugge, Shakhtar Donetsk, VfB Stuttgart

Away opponents: Real Madrid, Borussia Dortmund, Feyenoord, Slovan Bratislava

MD1: at Real Madrid, Tuesday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

Serie A's defending champions have continued their superb form early in 2026-27, pulling off three straight wins to open the campaign, including an absurd 3-2 home win over Napoli in which they trailed 2-1 at home with eight minutes remaining before Lautaro Martínez and Marcus Thuram completed an impressive comeback. This team just don't know when to quit; but will that carry over to European competition?

After a modest summer in which Denzel Dumfries (to Real Madrid) was really the only major loss, Christian Chivu's side are settled, experienced and know how to work together. Adding John Stones (from Man City) and Curtis Jones (from Liverpool) gives them valuable experience that should make a difference, but much will depend on Thuram and Martinez -- 40 goals between them last season -- to keep opponents under pressure.

8. LIVERPOOL

Home opponents: Atlético Madrid, FC Porto, Villarreal, Lens

Away opponents: Inter Milan, Club Brugge, Fenerbahce, LASK

MD1: vs. Atletico Madrid, Wednesday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

Nobody would deny that new manager Andoni Iraola is trying to make sense of a complete rebuild at Anfield since taking over from Arne Slot this summer, but Liverpool remain a team with more than enough talent to make a deep run in a short-form tournament like the Champions League. While they work things out in defense and midfield for the long slog of a domestic season, a star-studded first-team and gentler draw than their peers -- only their Pot 1 opponents, Atlético and Inter, will truly trouble -- should empower them to be a genuine threat in this competition.

New signing Barcola will slot into an attacking quartet with fellow summer arrival Víctor Muñoz and a pair of brilliant players (Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz) coming off difficult first seasons at Anfield. If they're on the same wavelength, and the likes of Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk continue to lead by example, the club have a chance. That said, we could easily be here in a couple of matchdays lamenting their form and wobbly defending, and that disconnect is informed by their lower ranking heading into the opening game.

9. ATLÉTICO MADRID

Home opponents: Bayern Munich, Man United, Fenerbahce, Viking FK

Away opponents: Liverpool, PSV Eindhoven, Bodo/Glimt, VfB Stuttgart

MD1: at Liverpool, Wednesday, 3 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. BST

It has been more than a decade since manager Diego Simeone had Atleti in the Champions League final, and our voters aren't bullish on them repeating that this season until we see their new-look squad take to the field in midweek. After the teary goodbye to Antoine Griezmann and a summer of fending off overtures from Barcelona and Arsenal to sign star striker Julián Álvarez, it's over to Simeone for his usual bag of motivational tricks and techniques if the third-best team in Spain are to do any better in Europe.

A slew of summer arrivals with big league backgrounds -- defender Cristian Romero (from Tottenham), playmaker Lee Kang-In (from PSG), wing back Alejandro Grimaldo (from Bayer Leverkusen) all joined on permanent deals, with Juventus forward Jonathan David making a deadline day loan move -- should be additive in nature even if it takes them a while to assimilate into Simeone's uncompromising style. That said, their draw is far from gentle and a fast start will be paramount if they are to rank in the top 10 next time around.

10. MANCHESTER UNITED

Home opponents: Bayern Munich, AS Roma, RB Leipzig, Sabah FK

Away opponents: Atlético Madrid, Sporting CP, Villarreal, Como

New permanent boss Michael Carrick has his work cut out to mold a consistently competitive team, especially with a schedule that will stretch a thin squad to its limits.

Borussia Dortmund, Napoli, Galatasaray, AS Roma, Como, Chelsea, Aston Villa, RB Leipzig.

stories.headline: Milwaukee Bucks offseason recap, early 2026-27 season preview
stories.summary: How will this roster fare in Season 1 without Giannis? We're recapping the offseason and taking an early look at 2026-27.
stories.body:
For the first time since 2012-13, the Milwaukee Bucks will enter a season without Giannis Antetokounmpo on the roster.

One of the league's biggest "will they/won't they" sagas finally ended just before the draft in June, when the Bucks sent the two-time MVP forward to the Miami Heat for a trade package headlined by guard Tyler Herro and a haul of draft picks.

How will this young roster fare in Season 1 post-Giannis? And are more moves on the way for Milwaukee?

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the 2026-27 season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for all 30 teams.

Quick links:

Roster | Depth chart | Transactions

More Bucks coverage | More NBA

Offseason at a glance
Key additions: Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, Caris LeVert

Key retentions: Gary Trent Jr.

Key subtractions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis

After 13 seasons, the Giannis era ended in Milwaukee with a mega trade to the Heat -- and the 2026-27 season will mark a major shift for the rebuilding franchise. The Bucks hired coach Taylor Jenkins to establish a culture. They added four new players from Miami, including former All-Star and Wisconsin native Tyler Herro, and selected Brayden Burries with the No. 10 pick in June. The Bucks will enter the season with an ill-fitting mix of players and low expectations, but they have the luxury to see what sticks long term. -- Jamal Collier

Zach Kram's offseason grade: B

In their long-awaited trade of Antetokounmpo, the Bucks landed a strong haul of draft picks and decently intriguing young players from Miami. Could they have set themselves up even better for the future if they'd traded their leading career scorer a year earlier? Probably. But taking this offseason in a vacuum, Milwaukee got its biggest move mostly right. -- Kram

What we learned over the past few months
From Ben Golliver's offseason lessons piece: The Giannis trade was only the beginning of Milwaukee's pain.

Let's be sure to extend maximum sympathy to Bucks fans, who are still processing Antetokounmpo's long-anticipated departure. It always hurts to lose a franchise icon, and this one is doubly painful because Milwaukee and Miami engaged in several playoff battles in recent years.

Though Antetokounmpo's exit was preceded by years of trade rumors, the Bucks didn't slide smoothly into a rebuilding effort. The good news: They sent Portis' contract to the Heat. The bad news: They haven't yet found a taker for Myles Turner, who was signed to a four-year, $107 million contract last summer in a failed attempt to appease Antetokounmpo. The really bad news: They inexplicably signed Trent to a four-year, $64 million contract this month after one of the worst seasons of his career, a deal that is already under investigation by the NBA. -- Golliver

The big question: What will define success this season?
The Bucks are in a rebuild but don't own their 2027 draft pick. (With changing lottery odds, tanking wouldn't make sense, anyway.) With up to 12 players having a case for legitimate playing time, will the franchise prioritize developing younger players such as Ryan Rollins and Burries, and turn the keys over to Herro, Turner and Trent to stay competitive in a deep Eastern Conference? The Bucks could be chasing a spot in the 9-10 play-in if all goes well. But in the post-Antetokounmpo era, the franchise will be looking to find a long-term direction. -- Collier

Basketball Power Index rank: No. 28
Here are the predicted Net Points per 100 possessions for the Bucks' top-seven players for the 2026-27 season:

I like to look at how often a team wins when a player plays over a long period of time. It captures quality and durability, albeit imperfectly. I was surprised that this new-look Bucks team had players whose sum of team wins ranked 17th leaguewide, ahead of teams such as the Minnesota Timberwolves and Dallas Mavericks. Based on this, I still think the Bucks will be bad, but not as bad as their 28th ranking in BPI. -- Dean Oliver

Read about how Net Points works here.

Biggest X factor
C Kel'el Ware

Of the four players Milwaukee acquired from Miami in the Antetokounmpo trade, Herro and Jaquez are mostly known quantities at this point, and 2025 first-round pick Jakucionis will have to fight for playing time with a big group of quality guards. But 2024 first-round pick Ware has untapped upside and a clearer path to playing time, with only veterans Turner and Kyle Kuzma currently ahead of him on the center/power forward depth chart.

Ware can score inside, make 3-pointers and protect the rim, but a lack of consistency meant he never fully gained Erik Spoelstra's trust in Miami. With the Bucks, he should have plenty of opportunity to find firmer footing as a foundational building block. -- Kram

Betting insight from our expert
Bet to make ahead of the season: Under 24.5 wins (+110)

The Bucks had a net rating of minus-7.7 points per game in 46 games without Antetokounmpo last season. Though this season's lineup will be different, the Bucks embraced a rebuild when they traded Antetokounmpo this offseason and last season's "without Giannis" numbers make a reasonable estimate of their expected level this season. During the past four NBA seasons, none of the 16 teams with point differentials worse than minus-7.5 won more than 22 games, with an average of 19.2 wins. -- André Snellings

Odds by DraftKings Sportsbook at time of publication.
